title: Piston ring

questions.q: How many rings do most automotive pistons have?
questions.answer: Most automotive pistons have three rings.

questions.q: What are the top two rings of an automotive piston primarily for?
questions.answer: The top two rings are primarily for compression sealing (compression rings), while also controlling oil.

questions.q: What is the lower ring of an automotive piston for?
questions.answer: The lower ring controls the supply of oil to the liner, lubricating the piston skirt and the compression rings (oil control rings).

questions.q: What cross section do typical compression ring designs have?
questions.answer: Typical compression ring designs have an essentially rectangular cross section or a keystone (right angled trapezoidal) cross section.

questions.q: What periphery profile does the top compression ring have?
questions.answer: The top compression ring has a barrel profile.

questions.q: What periphery profile does the second compression ring or scraper ring have?
questions.answer: The second compression ring or scraper ring has a taper napier form.

questions.answer: They split, creating two daughter nuclei and two or three more neutrons.

questions.q: What is created when neutrons from fission go on to split more nuclei?
questions.answer: A self-sustaining chain reaction is created.

questions.q: Where is a self-sustaining chain reaction controlled?
questions.answer: It is controlled in a nuclear reactor, or uncontrolled in a nuclear weapon.
